identity.title: EigenBench: A Comparative Behavioral Measure of Value Alignment

problem.claim: AI value alignment is an unsolved problem requiring quantitative assessment.

gap.claim: Existing metrics lack quantitative measures for comparatively assessing language-model alignment with subjective value systems.

contributions.claim: EigenBench is a black-box method that scores an ensemble of models against a specified constitution using scenario-based peer judgments aggregated with EigenTrust.
The method is designed for subjective values where ground-truth labels may not exist because reasonable judges can disagree.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors propose comparative value benchmarking that produces alignment scores without ground-truth labels, using weighted consensus across model judgments.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that EigenBench’s judgments align closely with human evaluators’ judgments on the same model ensemble.
The authors report that EigenBench recovers model rankings on GPQA without access to objective labels.

narrative_sequence.summary: Value alignment is framed as an unsolved problem, with a lack of quantitative metrics.
EigenBench scores models relative to a constitution from scenario judgments made by other ensemble members and aggregated with EigenTrust.
The framework omits ground-truth labels because subjective value judgments may reasonably differ.
Human-judgment agreement and recovery of GPQA rankings are presented as evidence of viability without objective labels.
The authors provide a code repository.

source_observation.claim: The abstract explicitly links the absence of ground truth to a consensus-based evaluation design, then reports comparison with human judgments.

lessons.interpretation: When labels are inherently contestable, making the evaluator aggregation rule explicit and testing its agreement with a relevant human reference can clarify what the metric measures.
lessons.application: For a subjective evaluation metric, define the judging population, aggregation procedure, and human-reference comparison alongside the score definition.
lessons.exception: This move is unsuitable when the task has authoritative objective labels or when human judgments are not an appropriate reference.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the constitution, scenario dataset, ensemble size, scoring scale, or quantitative closeness to human judgments.
Details of the GPQA ranking-recovery setup and comparison baselines are not given.
The abstract does not establish independent validity, reproducibility, or priority of the proposed method.
